name: clean_chutes
summary: Remove chute pieces no item can pass through to a consumer; a junction, overflow or splitter left with one way in and out becomes a straight or corner. Select by network_id, reference_ids or a min/max box. Pieces holding items stay. Dry run by default; confirm to run.

help.text: Judges whole chute networks, even when only some pieces are selected; only selected pieces change. Kit (Chute) pays and takes back; a replacement keeps paint and owner. The report is clean_cables' (target minimal): pieces lists each removal (operation remove_dead_chute, with why) and each swap (simplify_junction, with connected_ends); dead_end_pieces the dead pieces that stay, with stopped_by; kept_pieces each piece on a path left with an open end, with why; riding the pieces that hold items.
help.keys: job_id, status, ready, problems [], pieces [], by_prefab [], kept_pieces [], swapped [], removed [], not_swapped [], refund [], preflight_summary, final_check, verification, gas_check, error.

dead.text: Items move one way through a chute: a straight or corner passes them on, a junction merges its inputs into its output, an overflow or splitter sends them to its outputs. A piece serves a path when an item can reach it from a source and go on from it to a consumer. Sources: a device port that pushes items out (a sorter or stacker output, a chute bin, an inlet), a two-way rocket umbilical port, and any piece an item rides in. Consumers: a device port that takes items (a machine input, an export bin, an outlet) and two-way ports. An open end is no consumer: what leaves through it falls on the floor. why names the cause: orphan (joined to nothing), no_consumer or no_source. Devices are never removed and count by their ports whatever feeds them; a closed valve counts as open.

open_ends.summary: No end left where items fall out.
open_ends.text: A dead piece stays (stopped_by would_drop_items) when a piece or chute device that stays would push items into it, and so may the dead pieces behind it. The exception is a junction, overflow or splitter on a path: it becomes a straight or corner without that end in the same run. One with an end that already leads nowhere becomes a plain piece too; one left whole is in kept_pieces with no_plain_piece, keep_ids or item_riding. An overflow left open to spill on the floor counts as dead: spare it with keep_ids.

riding.text: The game destroys an item with the chute it rides in, so a piece holding an item is never removed or replaced. riding skip (the default) leaves it, and the dead pieces it would push the item into, and runs the rest; riding refuse refuses the whole run with items_riding while any piece it would change holds one. The riding list names each piece, what it carries and what happens to it (kept or not_simplified). A dry run only reports. Let the item pass, or take it out with move_item, and run again.

reference_id.description: A device or piece on the network.

network_id.description: A chute network, every piece of it (see networks).

reference_ids.description: Chute pieces to clean, up to 4096; only they change.

min.description: Box corner, [x, y, z] in metres; with max: every chute piece in the box.

max.description: The other corner; at most a 32 m cube.

keep_ids.description: Pieces never removed or replaced; the dead pieces they would push items into stay too.

riding.description: A piece holding an item: skip leaves it and runs the rest (default); refuse refuses the run (topic riding).

from_id.description: The thing whose slots pay and take the refund; default the player (see swaps/materials).

refund.description: Give back kits for removed pieces and cheaper replacements. Default true; false is refund_to none.

job_id.description: Poll a confirmed run; give nothing else.
